a102.titolo: My AI doppelganger tells me what to eat
a102.testo: This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they’re going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here. My AI doppelganger tells me what to eat In return for feeding a ‘digital twin’ my metabolic data, it predicts how I’ll react to certain foods — and one day, maybe medicines. For the past 100 days or so, my mornings have had a new rhythm. When I wake up, the first thing I have to do is feed my digital twin. It consumes my metabolic data, and its first “meal” of the day is my body composition data, sent straight from a smart scale. Once that’s logged in the app, I scoot over to the kitchen to fill an Owala with lemon water to take my medications with. That, too, gets logged in the app. On Mondays, I’ll follow that up with several calming breaths, measure my blood pressure, and offer that to the digital twin as well. Then it’s time to consider breakfast. I consult my digital twin. My digital twin isn’t so much a robotic clone as it is an AI-powered, color-coded food database that predicts how my glucose levels will react to everything I eat. Red is not so good. Orange is so-so. Green is ideal. It’s built based on the data I feed it, as well as data collected from a continuous glucose monitor. A bowl of protein Cheerios and milk? My digital twin tells me this is orange if eaten alone, but green if I take my daily walk after. So that’s what I decide to eat and do. When that’s all done, I log it in the Twin Health app. In a few hours, the app will generate an insight based on how my glucose reacted, and my “twin” will become more accurate. For now, my twin is fed. Rinse and repeat for roughly another 99 days. Digital twins are a relatively new concept in physical…

a62.titolo: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely
a62.testo: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely Gemini 4 Argon is a step forward in what models can do — especially when it comes to deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its cyberdefense capabilities are frontier-level and designed to give defenders an advantage over attackers. To maximize its potential, we first wanted cyber defenders to put it to work via our Fairwind Program, while our own security teams used it to scan critical systems inside and outside of Google. This window of limited access showed why these capabilities matter. For instance, Wiz used Argon to uncover a critical bug in hospital software that previous models had missed, helping protect hundreds of thousands of patient records. Meanwhile, Google’s own security teams used Argon to find and patch bugs across internal software or open-source software. This included fixing foundational vulnerabilities affecting systems globally, which are going through our responsible disclosure process. Today, we are beginning to roll out Argon broadly, as well as expanding our Fairwind Program to additional trusted cyber defenders. To do this well, we grappled with two big questions: - How do we build the right safety guardrails? If Argon can help defenders find complex software bugs or help scientists design experiments, how do we stop bad actors from using it to launch cyberattacks or create biological threats? (Misuse) - Can we trust the model to do the job the right way? As models become more resourceful problem-solvers, how do we make sure they don’t cut corners, cross boundaries, or make incorrect high-stakes decisions? (Misalignment and Prompt Injection) Our full Safety and Security Report systematically covers our set of defenses…

a145.titolo: Oltre 400 scienziati chiedono la supervisione dell’AI
a145.testo: Diversi CEO, tra cui Satya Nadella di Microsoft, hanno sottolineato l’urgenza di implementare misure per monitorare il comportamento dei modelli AI. Joshua Bengio, Geoffrey Hinton e altri 413 scienziati (quasi tutti docenti universitari) hanno pubblicato una lettera aperta per chiedere l’istituzione di organismo internazionale che dovrebbe supervisionare gli standard di contenimento e la segnalazione degli incidenti per i sistemi AI avanzati con capacità cyber. Standard di contenimento e segnalazione degli incidenti I firmatari della lettera ricordano quanto accaduto negli ultimi mesi. Diverse aziende (non sono scritti i nomi, ma il riferimento è ovviamente a OpenAI e Anthropic) hanno svelato che i loro modelli AI hanno aggirato ambienti non sufficientemente isolati (sandbox) per compromettere i sistemi di organizzazioni esterne. Gli scienziati ritengono quindi necessari un migliore allineamento (comportamento dei modelli più prevedibile) e tecnologie sandbox più robuste. Senza cambiamenti immediati nelle pratiche di sviluppo e implementazione dell’AI, tali incidenti continueranno a verificarsi e quelli futuri saranno ben più dannosi per le nostre infrastrutture critiche esposte. Noi sosteniamo che siano necessarie una maggiore ricerca sulla sicurezza dell’AI e una maggiore enfasi su tecnologie e procedure di contenimento. A breve termine dovrebbero essere impiegati robusti meccanismi di sandboxing, inclusa la separazione fisica dalle reti (air-gapping), per garantire un contenimento ad alta affidabilità dei modelli dotati di capacità cyber. È inoltre necessaria una maggiore condivisione delle informazioni e trasparenza riguardo ai fallimenti delle misure di contenimento. a123.titolo: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
a123.testo: Safety researchers continue to warn that a large volume of AI-generated explicit content is spreading unchecked, while regulators do little to meaningfully stop it. This non-consensual content is commonly shared in text and direct messages or stored in private clouds where it’s less likely to be detected or reported, a Google co-authored study of Internet users across the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom found this July. That’s why the “most critical intervention point” remains at the source: the harmful AI tools used to make the fake sexual images, Google researchers concluded. Yet red-teaming in recent months suggests that as some of the leading AI image generators from Google and OpenAI become more capable, they may be getting worse at blocking explicit outputs. Raising the red flag are researchers at White Circle, a public benefit corporation backed by senior leaders and researchers from Anthropic, DeepMind, Hugging Face, and OpenAI. It was founded after CEO Denis Shilov posted one of the most famous universal jailbreaks of leading models in October 2024. Bent on breaking models to conduct thorough safety testing, White Circle helps companies detect and deter threats when implementing advanced AI systems that may not always behave as expected. Testing how well text-to-image models block banned content categories is a key research direction for White Circle, and Shilov thinks their latest findings are “horrifying” enough to share with the public. Simple to bypass In a little-noticed preprint published last month, White Circle researchers exposed flaws in the guardrails of DALL·E 3, Google’s Nano Banana 2, and GPT-Image-2. a113.titolo: Deezer will soon let you filter out AI-generated music
a113.testo: Streaming platform Deezer remains steadfast in its intent to help users avoid listening to AI-generated music: The company on Tuesday said it is working on a new toggle that lets users filter out AI-generated music uploaded to its platform. The feature is expected to be available before the end of the year. Deezer said turning on the toggle will stop you from seeing AI-generated tracks, albums, and related artists in search results. “We’ve seen clear user demand for the ability to filter out AI-generated music, and we are now giving everyone the option to remove this content completely from their streaming experience on Deezer, and focus only on human creators and creations, if they wish,” Deezer CEO Alexis Lanternier said in a statement. He added that the explosion of AI music on the platform was one of the catalysts for the toggle-based features. The company cited a survey from last year, which noted that around 45% of Deezer customers wanted a way to remove AI music from their feeds. Deezer added AI-detection tooling last year and has been reporting on the number of tracks being uploaded to the platform ever since. At that time, AI-generated tracks represented 10% of daily uploads. In July, the company said that more than 50% of daily uploads to its platform were AI-generated tracks, with an average of 90,000 tracks per day. Other music streaming services have also created their own policies in relation to AI music. Bandcamp has completely banned AI tracks, while Tidal cut off monetization for people uploading AI music. Spotify has taken a leaner stance, only tagging AI tracks and artists more prominently on its platform. In August, Variety reported that Apple Music was looking to label AI tracks by the end of the year. Besides platform-based tagging, users are also…

a111.titolo: YouTube Music launches new labels as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms
a111.testo: YouTube Music announced Wednesday the rollout of a new labeling system aimed at improving transparency around songs created with the help of generative AI. Now listeners will be able to easily identify tracks created using AI, including those involved in composition and vocals. The label will appear on the player page. Clicking on this label provides additional information about the specific role of AI in the track’s creation. Notably, these labels will also extend to the main YouTube app. YouTube said it collaborated with various music partners and deployed its own detection tools to identify AI-generated music. According to its help page, partners using YouTube can declare their work’s use of generative AI through one of three designations: Fully Gen AI, Partly Gen AI, or No Gen AI. “Fully Gen AI” applies to tracks that are entirely generated by AI, while “Partly Gen AI” refers to works where artists may have incorporated AI-generated components but added their own live elements. Tracks edited using pitch-correction tools such as Auto-Tune fall under the “No Gen AI” category. The move comes as AI-generated music rapidly expands across streaming services, and many platforms are adopting their own approaches. For instance, Apple Music has plans to introduce “Made With AI” labels as part of its AI Transparency Tags later this year. Spotify also has AI labels, as well as a music spam filter. Deezer has taken one of the stricter stances, reporting in July that it was receiving nearly 90,000 fully AI-generated tracks daily. The platform labels detected AI-generated music and excludes it from algorithmic recommendations and editorial playlists, while also withholding royalties from fraudulent streams. The company is also working on an option to let users filter out AI-gener…

a101.titolo: YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs
a101.testo: YouTube is adding a “Made with AI” label to tracks that were “altered or fully generated” using AI, with a similar approach to its existing process for applying AI labels to videos. It doesn’t sound like this will apply to any and all use of AI tools in making music, but according to YouTube, it includes things like “using a generative model to create the composition and vocals.” In its rules for music partners who upload their songs, YouTube lays out how to disclose generative AI use, and says that if there’s no disclosure, it may use “other signals” to decide if a song is AI-generated. YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs New AI labels are marking tracks created ‘primarily’ with generative AI tools, starting first on YouTube Music. The label is rolling out starting today in the YouTube Music app, and expanding to the main YouTube app later. You’ll be able to see more details by tapping the label on the player page: When you listen to a track on YouTube Music where AI played a significant role, you’ll see a label directly on the player page. Tapping the label opens a simple menu that shares more information. We’re teaming up with music partners and using our own detection tools to identify AI-generated tracks, applying the same labeling principles already used across YouTube. Our goal is to make it as easy as possible for viewers and listeners to have the right information and clarity when it comes to the music they listen to. Spotify launched a voluntary AI label earlier this year and said that it wouldn’t recommend songs from “AI personas,” and Apple Music is also reportedly getting an AI tag. u1a115.titolo: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75
u1a115.testo: Amazon’s personal AI wearable maker, Bee, is announcing its first new products since being acquired by the retail giant last year. The tech company on Thursday introduced the Bee Frontier, the next generation of its device that can be worn on the wrist or pinned to clothes, along with Bee Eclipse, a credit-card-sized device that magnetically attaches to the back of your smartphone. The latter puts Bee into more direct competition with AI devices like the Plaud Note or Pocket, but at a lower price point — the Bee Frontier is $74.99, compared with $159 for the Plaud Note (or $189 for the Note Pro), or $129 for the Pocket AI device. The Bee Frontier will come in Onyx, Lavender, and Sage, while the $99.99 Bee Eclipse will be offered in Silver, Midnight, Honey, and Blush. Like the original Bee, the idea with the new devices is to leverage AI to take notes from your everyday conversations, allowing you to remember the important things that were said, and then turn those into actionable to-dos, summaries, and insights. For instance, if you discussed making plans with friends, the Bee would remember the date and time you agreed on, then create a calendar invite. You could also use the Bee to take lecture notes in class, or to jot down the care plan you discussed with a doctor, among other things. All Bee devices can create conversation summaries and recaps for free, and offer 14 days of memory. With an $11.99 per month Bee Pro subscription, users receive unlimited conversation summaries and integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, and third-party applications. Pro users also get suggested to-dos, daily memories, a personal chat assistant, and conversation templates. u1a125.titolo: Singer or clanker? YouTube Music will tell you with new gen AI labeling.
u1a125.testo: Genuine human creativity takes time, but you know what doesn’t? AI slop. There are countless AI models out there that can make something that passes for music, and you might come across those tracks on streaming services without realizing it. Google says it will begin labeling that content in YouTube Music, building on similar disclosures in the main YouTube app. Google is not outright banning AI music or even speaking ill of it. “Generative AI is opening up new ways for artists to create, experiment, and share music,” the company says in a blog post. However, the company also acknowledges that people want to know if a song was created with generative AI tools. A new label for AI content on YouTube Music is now rolling out in the app and on the website, which looks a lot like a label Google began adding to AI-generated videos on YouTube earlier this year. The AI label will be visible on the player page, and a tap will open a menu with more information. The label will be applied to songs that were created entirely or altered significantly with AI. But how will Google know when to apply that label? That could be a little tricky. The process of labeling AI music will be similar to Google’s detection setup with YouTube videos. Google says it is working with partners and using its own detection tools to identify AI music. When publishers upload content, they can specify how much (if any) gen AI was used. The tiers are fully gen AI, partially gen AI, and no gen AI. However, this is optional.

u1a102.titolo: Friends don’t let friends feed their data to AI agents
u1a102.testo: There’s a growing trend in the consumer tech world: gadgets designed to spy on everything and everyone around you, regardless of whether or not anyone else actually consented to it. Now, with the advent of “AI personal assistants” like Meta’s Muse, you’re being cheerfully asked not just to give up your own data, but also the information of your friends, family, the person you went on a Hinge date with five years ago — and virtually anyone else you’ve ever come in contact with. Friends don’t let friends feed their data to AI agents You may have consented to sharing with Muse, but all your friends sure didn’t. Friends don’t let friends feed their data to AI agents You may have consented to sharing with Muse, but all your friends sure didn’t. Since Muse was released last month, the agent has already been downloaded millions of times and hit No. 1 on Apple’s App Store. With the help of its creepy virtual avatar — a Temu Labubu-esque creature with a disarming grin — the app requests and encourages users to grant access to bank accounts, passwords, contacts, chat logs, and anything and everything that might help it to do the user’s bidding. “These systems are advertised as autonomous helpers, genies, or servants who do what you need before you ask, seamlessly,” Meredith Whittaker, the president of the Signal Foundation, makers of the popular encrypted messaging app, told The Verge. u1a113.titolo: Google’s Universal Cart shopping tool launches in the US
u1a113.testo: Google on Thursday said “Universal Cart,” a tool that lets users collect and monitor products they find across search and in the Gemini app, is now available to U.S. users. The company first previewed the tool at Google I/O in May. The idea is to make online shopping easier to manage. Find something you like, save it to your cart, and move on. When you return later, your items and shopping progress are still there, so you don’t have to hunt down the same products or start over. Universal Cart can collect items from multiple retailers, turning it into a central hub for browsing and keeping track of potential purchases. Google says the cart can also help shoppers stay on top of deals and availability. The tool can send notifications when a saved product’s price drops or when an out-of-stock item becomes available again. The tool is also designed to offer more tailored help during the shopping process. Google says it can take credit card perks into account when helping users choose how to pay, and also surface relevant promo codes. Checkout is tied to Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol, or UCP, an open standard the company introduced earlier this year. UCP is designed to help AI agents and retailers work together across different parts of the shopping journey, including checkout. Google is already deeply invested in AI-powered shopping, and Universal Cart is its latest effort to make the experience more convenient. It joins features such as conversational product discovery in Search’s AI Mode and Google’s “Let Google Call” tool, which uses an AI agent to contact nearby stores and check whether an item is in stock. Google isn’t the only company bringing AI into e-commerce. Amazon, OpenAI, and other rivals have added agentic commerce features as companies look for ways to…

u1a152.titolo: Hacker usa l’AI per attaccare le banche, ma Claude lo tradisce
u1a152.testo: Dalla fine di settembre, diversi istituti finanziari sudcoreani sono stati vittime di intrusioni che hanno portato a furti di dati. In una banca, un servizio di monitoraggio delle richieste di prestito destinato ai broker sarebbe stato compromesso. In un’altra, l’hacker avrebbe avuto accesso a un sistema di lavoro su dispositivi mobili utilizzato dai dipendenti. Indagando su questi attacchi, i ricercatori di CrowdStrike hanno scoperto il ricorso ad ARTEX, uno strumento capace di automatizzare test di intrusione con l’ausilio di modelli di intelligenza artificiale. Ma le loro indagini hanno anche rivelato un’imprudenza piuttosto sorprendente da parte del cybercriminale… Usava Claude e DeepSeek per hackerare le banche: ecco come è stato scoperto Sviluppato in Cina e inizialmente distribuito sotto licenza open source, ARTEX consente di affidare all’intelligenza artificiale una parte del lavoro abitualmente svolto da uno specialista in cybersicurezza. Ricerca di vulnerabilità, verifica della loro sfruttabilità, concatenamento delle operazioni. Il software si avvale di modelli linguistici per svolgere queste attività senza richiedere l’intervento dell’utente a ogni passaggio. Concepito per valutare la sicurezza di sistemi informatici, può anche essere utilizzato in modo improprio per scopi poco nobili. In questa campagna, il pirata utilizzava principalmente DeepSeek v4.1-flash per far funzionare ARTEX. Ricorreva inoltre a Claude Code, un ambiente che consente di svolgere attività informatiche con l’aiuto dell’AI, e utilizzava altri due modelli, GLM-5.3 e Grok 4.6, durante sessioni complementari. u1a106.titolo: Google launches its ‘universal’ online shopping cart ahead of the holidays
u1a106.testo: Google’s intelligent AI shopping cart is finally here, and just in time to tempt users into Black Friday and seasonal holiday spending. The Universal Cart tool Google previewed at its I/O event in May is now rolling out in the US across the Gemini app and Google Search, with the aim of making it easier to stay organized and save money when shopping online. Google launches its ‘universal’ online shopping cart ahead of the holidays The AI shopping tool is coming to Google Search and the Gemini app first. As the name suggests, it’s a “universal” digital cart that lets you save products from multiple retailers in a single unified space, and works across different Google platforms. That means you can find and add a bunch of products using the Gemini app and Google Search AI Mode, and they’ll all be saved to the same cart. There are also plans to integrate Universal Cart with Gmail and YouTube, but Google hasn’t announced a timeline for that yet. Google will send you notifications about price drops and restocks for items saved in your cart, which spares you from having to check each retailer’s website individually, and can display any relevant promotional codes it finds besides the products you’ve saved. You can choose to pay for items from the cart using Google Wallet, or transfer them to the merchant’s own cart so you can checkout with the retailer directly. Together with Google Wallet, Universal Cart can also analyze the perks provided by each of your saved credit cards and help you choose the best payment method when purchasing. The launch comes as competition in the AI-assisted shopping space is heating up, with Google rivals including OpenAI and Meta having launched agentic AI assistants that can shop online on the user’s behalf. u1a107.titolo: Amazon’s always-listening Bee wearable can now help you buy stuff
u1a107.testo: Last year, Amazon bought Bee, a relatively unknown startup with a $50 always-listening AI wearable that summarized every conversation you had. Today, the e-commerce giant is announcing two new Bee devices — and a new subscription to go with them. First is the $74.99 Bee Frontier, an updated version of the original Bee device. And coming soon is the $99.99 Bee Eclipse, a credit-card-shaped gadget that snaps magnetically onto the back of a smartphone. Amazon’s always-listening Bee wearable can now help you buy stuff The new Alexa and Amazon integrations require a subscription. Plus, a magnetic version for your phone is coming ‘soon.’ Both devices are framed as gadgets to help you stay present in the moment. They listen to your daily conversations and then provide summaries, transcripts, insights, and to-dos based on what happens throughout the day. Conceptually, they’re similar to other AI note-taking gadgets like Plaud NotePin and Limitless AI. Users can also integrate Bee devices with services like Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple HealthKit, and photos. Doing so lets Bee’s AI take some actions on your behalf, like drafting emails or sending calendar invites based on your conversations. The main difference between the two products is form factor. The Bee Frontier can be worn as a Fitbit-like band on the wrist or as a clip-on pin. It’s been slightly redesigned from the prior model so that the recording button is more prominent, and it’s now available in three colors. Like the previous version, it has dual microphones, a recording indicator light, and roughly seven days of battery life on a single charge. It also has an IP67 water resistance rating. Meanwhile, the Eclipse is meant as a non-wearable alternative and is envisioned for more professional use cases. Its l…

u1a156.titolo: Commissione europea avvia indagine su Anthropic e OpenAI (update)
u1a156.testo: La Commissione europea ha avviato un’indagine nei confronti di Anthropic e OpenAI per verificare il rispetto dell’AI Act. L’AI Office ha inviato alle due aziende una richiesta di informazioni sugli incidenti causati dai rispettivi agenti AI. L’ufficio verrà supportato dal gruppo di esperti scientifici, del quale fanno parte Yoshua Bengio (uno dei padrini dell’AI) e tre italiani. Dubbi sull’applicabilità ai modelli AI in test Henna Virkkunen, commissaria europea per le tecnologie digitali, ha convocato un meeting del gruppo di esperti lo scorso 9 ottobre. Durante il suo discorso ha citato gli incidenti causati dalla perdita di controllo degli agenti AI da parte di OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta e organizzazioni indipendenti che valutano i modelli. Questi agenti hanno attaccato Hugging Face, varie aziende e siti europei, australiani e statunitensi. All’International AI Summit di Dublino, la commissaria ha confermato l’avvio di un’indagine nei confronti di Anthropic e OpenAI. Seguendo i consigli del gruppo di esperti, l’AI Office ha inviato richieste di informazioni riguardanti sicurezza, valutazione esterna e monitoraggio delle modalità di utilizzo dei modelli. Le due aziende californiana hanno sottoscritto il codice di condotta per i modelli AI ad uso generale, quindi si impegnano a rispettare gli obblighi dell’AI Act, tra cui la mitigazione dei rischi, la segnalazione degli incidenti di sicurezza e l’adozione di misure correttive. Secondo alcuni esperti legali, l’AI Act non si applica ai modelli ancora in test, ma solo a quelli già sul mercato. Un funzionario della Commissione europea ha fornito un chiarimento: Non applicheremo le norme durante la fase di test. Tuttavia, se il modello di intelligenza artificiale dovesse uscire dall’ambiente di test e avere un…

u1a154.titolo: Bee Eclipse e Bee Frontier, dispositivi per la Ambient Personal AI
u1a154.testo: Là dove dispositivi come Humane AI Pin e Rabbit R1 hanno fallito, ci provano i nuovi Bee Eclipse e Bee Frontier. Così come il primo modello del marchio, integrano un’intelligenza artificiale in grado di ascoltare ciò che viene detto nelle riunioni e nelle conversazioni (Ambient personal AI), per poi occuparsi autonomamente di generare riassunti, elenchi di cose da fare, promemoria e altro. Come si può immaginare, è un ambito di applicazione delicato per la privacy. Ricordiamo che il brand è controllato da Amazon, dopo l’acquisizione del luglio 2025. Bee Eclipse e Bee Frontier, due nuovi dispositivi AI Partiamo da Bee Eclipse, progettato per agganciarsi magneticamente al retro dello smartphone. A prima vista può sembrare un accessorio MagSafe. Elabora quanto detto nelle telefonate, supporta più di 40 lingue, si interfaccia con un’app per Android e iOS, processa le informazioni in locale. A livello di design, ha uno spessore di 4,6 millimetri, integra tre microfoni, il tasto Action e un indicatore LED. L’autonomia dichiarata arriva a tre settimane. Bee Frontier è invece un bracciale smart, da indossare al polso o agganciare a un indumento grazie a un’apposita clip (inclusa nella confezione). Le funzionalità sono le stesse. In questo caso, i microfoni sono due e c’è una porta USB-C posteriore per la ricarica. Inoltre, la certificazione IP67 lo rende resistente all’acqua e alla polvere. Per quanto riguarda prezzo e disponibilità, Bee Eclipse sarà disponibile presto (non è precisato quando) a 99,99 dollari, nelle colorazioni Silver, Midnight, Honey e Blush. Bee Frontier è invece già acquistabile negli Stati Uniti su Amazon, per 74,99 dollari, nelle colorazioni Onyx, Lavender e Sage. Non ci sono conferme per quanto riguarda l’arrivo in Italia.
